recognize_zh: CT 可見視丘占位病灶（箭頭），切片為成片的大型漿母細胞樣/免疫母細胞樣淋巴瘤細胞，核偏位、核仁明顯、細胞質豐富；免疫染色 B 細胞標記陰性、多個核染色陽性且 Ki-67 極高，符合腔外型原發性滲出性淋巴瘤（extracavitary PEL）。
features: CT (A): mass lesion in the thalamus/deep gray matter (arrowhead) with surrounding hypodensity
H&E low power (B): diffuse sheets of discohesive lymphoid cells in brain parenchyma
H&E high power (C): large cells with round, eccentric nuclei, prominent nucleoli and moderate to abundant amphophilic cytoplasm (plasmablastic/immunoblastic)
IHC (D, H): largely negative or only focal/membranous staining in tumor cells
Nuclear stains (E, F, G) diffusely positive in tumor cells; chromogenic ISH (I, red) positive in many nuclei
Proliferation stain (J): very high nuclear positivity
describe_en: Composite figure. Axial CT shows a thalamic mass lesion. Biopsy shows brain parenchyma diffusely infiltrated by sheets of large discohesive cells with eccentric round nuclei, prominent nucleoli and abundant amphophilic cytoplasm, imparting a plasmablastic/immunoblastic appearance. The immunostain panel shows negative or weak staining with some markers, diffuse nuclear positivity with several nuclear markers, positive red-chromogen in situ hybridization in many nuclei, and a very high proliferation index. The individual markers are not labeled in the image; in the clinical context the findings are consistent with extracavitary primary effusion lymphoma (HHV8-positive, frequently EBV-positive) presenting as a thalamic mass.

ddx.vs: Plasmablastic lymphoma is morphologically similar and EBER+ but HHV8/LANA-negative, whereas PEL is HHV8/LANA-positive.

ddx.dx: Primary CNS diffuse large B-cell lymphoma
ddx.vs: PCNSL is angiocentric and expresses CD20/PAX5 with an ABC phenotype, and is HHV8-negative.
Myeloma shows light-chain-restricted cytoplasmic immunoglobulin and CD138/CD56, and is HHV8- and EBV-negative.
HHV8+ DLBCL usually arises with multicentric Castleman disease, expresses IgM lambda and is EBV-negative, unlike typically EBV+ immunoglobulin-null PEL.

stain: CT; H&E; IHC panel; ISH (red chromogen)
